turns.content: Records of benzene alkylation with ethylene show higher C8 selectivity for MFI-type solids than for homogeneous acids. Summarize that observed association, noting that acidity, site density, conversion, residence time, and transport were not matched.
What causal claim, if any, follows from that comparison alone? What controls would be needed to show that catalyst heterogeneity itself causes the selectivity difference?
Set up a mechanistic comparison of pore-shape effects, acidity, activity, and mass transport that could explain the C8 preference.
What calculations or measurements would compare formation and diffusion of ethylbenzene with more highly alkylated aromatics inside an MFI pore network?
In benzene alkylation with ethylene, identify the C8 hydrocarbon product and its degree of alkylation.
Which structural feature of MFI zeolites such as ZSM-5 is most relevant to selectivity in aromatic alkylation?
Compare the steric and diffusion behavior of ethylbenzene with bulkier, more highly alkylated aromatics in those pores.
Why are catalyst heterogeneity, lower acidity, or lower overall activity alone insufficient explanations for the selectivity difference?
Synthesize the structural and mechanistic evidence into the best-supported explanation for the C8 preference.
State the evidentiary limits imposed by the absence of pore-dimension, matched-acidity, rate, transport, and causal-design data.
Give the final mechanistic explanation and separately qualify what the observational comparison does and does not establish causally.
